name: Opening range (NY 30-minute)

definitions.definition_text: When ICT talks about the opening range: from 9:30 to traditionally about 10:00 — about 30 minutes. Inside that 30 minutes he measures willingness for price (wherever it opens) to get back to the previous session close if it's a gap down.
conditions: Measured once market starts trading at 9:30
Gap-down case: willingness to reprice to previous session close in first 30 minutes
invalidation: If no immediate willingness to reprice back to previous session close on a gap down → described as extremely bearish; attention turns to deeper discount objectives on 15m / hourly / daily
definitions.variations_note: Defines opening range strictly as NY 9:30–10:00 measurement window for gap-fill willingness.

definitions.definition_text: The first 30 minutes of trading is the opening range — not a 15-minute opening range, not the ORB / 5-minute ORB people talk about. That first 30 minutes gives the rhyme and reason for the entire morning session.
conditions: Focus on first 30 minutes after open as the important time window
definitions.timeframe_session_context: NY morning; first 30 minutes of trading; explicitly rejects 15m/5m ORB framing
definitions.variations_note: Same 30m NY OR definition as uwFJ0t7SAOU, with explicit rejection of retail ORB lengths and morning-session tone claim.

definitions.definition_text: Pre-market range is NOT the opening range. The opening range is the first 30 minutes after the opening bell at the New York session (post 9:30 to 10:00). There is no 15-minute opening range; it's a 30-minute opening range — algorithmic.
conditions: NY session opening bell defines the OR window
definitions.timeframe_session_context: NY local / Eastern; 9:30–10:00 contrasted with pre-market windows
definitions.variations_note: Aligns with NY 30m OR; same video ALSO uses 'opening range' for post-premarket hourly slots (see opening_range_hourly_model) — CONFLICTING_SOURCES status on this concept_id.

definitions.definition_text: First hour's range / first hour's dealing range is NOT the opening range, which is 30 minutes.

When using opening ranges (not silver bullet): opening ranges are defined by 30 minutes — not 15 minutes, not 5 minutes. Same 30-minute application for London session and for 9:30–10:00 when trading indices; retail 15-minute focus called limiting.
conditions: Applies to NY 9:30–10:00 indices and London-timed OR analogue
definitions.timeframe_session_context: NY 9:30–10:00 and London 30m OR windows; contrasted with silver-bullet hour
definitions.variations_note: Official ICT reinforcement of 30m OR; KEEP DISTINCT from silver-bullet 10:00–11:00 FPFVG framing in same video.

source.title: ICT Opening Range Theory \ 1st Presented FVG Logic

definitions.definition_text: Judas swing forms at 9:30 to 10 o'clock — that is your opening range (time window). In the same lecture, opening range gap is separately defined as Friday close → Monday 9:30 open difference.
conditions: NY 9:30–10:00 window labeled opening range / Judas
definitions.timeframe_session_context: NY AM 9:30–10:00 Judas / OR time window
definitions.variations_note: KEEP SEPARATE from ORG gap geometry in same video — opening range ≠ opening range gap. Reinforces 30m NY OR clock while proving naming collision risk.

source.title: 2023 ICT Mentorship - Opening Range Gap Repricing Macro

definitions.definition_text: Opening range in the morning session specifically aimed at 9:30 to 10:00 — the 30-minute algorithmic opening range. There is no other opening range except for that 30-minute interval; if less than 30 minutes it is not algorithmic.
conditions: 30-minute length required for algorithmic OR claim
invalidation: Sub-30m OR framing rejected as non-algorithmic
definitions.timeframe_session_context: NY AM 9:30–10:00; lecture also maps same logic to midnight
definitions.variations_note: Strong official reinforcement of 30m NY OR. CONFLICTS with Month 10 index 1h OR (ORbtHOUzAIM 9:30–10:30) — keep both; see opening_range_index_futures_1h.
